instruction:
Software launch locations: LibreCAD: `/usr/bin/librecad`; FreeCAD: `/usr/bin/freecad`; KiCad: `/home/user/Applications/kicad-10.0.2/kicad-10.0.2-x86_64.AppImage`; Blender: `/home/user/Applications/blender-4.2.3-linux-x64/blender`. Required four-software transfer workflow: LibreCAD -> FreeCAD -> KiCad -> Blender. Start from the provided seed DXF /home/user/Desktop/seed_sensor_node_enclosure.dxf; do not start from a blank or unrelated drawing. This is a chained workflow: every later stage must read an artifact from the previous stage, and every required intermediate file must be saved on the Desktop. The design token for this task is EW4G01; keep this token visible in the DXF labels and KiCad silkscreen. The Blender output must visibly consume the stage-2 STL and stage-3 SVG through Blender's native import/export operations.

Design goal: DIN rail sensor node enclosure with USB and LED windows. This case is intentionally different from the other benchmark cases: domain=industrial_iot_enclosure, mechanical target=an assembled enclosure with visible USB window and two translucent LED lenses, electronics target=a sensor-node PCB with USB-C connector, MCU, sensor header, and two LED footprints.

1. LibreCAD stage: open the provided seed file /home/user/Desktop/seed_sensor_node_enclosure.dxf in LibreCAD, use it as the starting drawing, complete the required 2D geometry, remove all GUIDE construction entities, and save /home/user/Desktop/stage1_sensor_node_enclosure.dxf. Use millimeters. Use layers OUTLINE, PORT, HOLE, LABEL. The overall drawing envelope must be 92 mm x 58 mm. Include the required circular features: center (8,8) radius 2.2; center (84,8) radius 2.2; center (8,50) radius 2.2; center (84,50) radius 2.2; center (72,29) radius 1.6; center (80,29) radius 1.6. Add readable labels EW4G01, USB-C, LED-A, LED-B on the LABEL layer.
2. FreeCAD stage: import /home/user/Desktop/stage1_sensor_node_enclosure.dxf in FreeCAD. Create the 3D mechanical body from that LibreCAD DXF, and export the body as /home/user/Desktop/stage2_sensor_node_enclosure.stl with an approximate bounding size of 92 mm x 58 mm x 22 mm. Then, from the same FreeCAD model, export a top-face or board-interface outline for KiCad as /home/user/Desktop/stage2_sensor_node_enclosure_handoff_outline.dxf. This handoff DXF must represent the same XY envelope as the FreeCAD body and include the visible labels FREECAD_TO_KICAD and EW4G01.
3. KiCad stage: open KiCad, create a PCB from /home/user/Desktop/stage2_sensor_node_enclosure_handoff_outline.dxf by importing the handoff DXF as the Edge.Cuts board outline, and save the KiCad board as /home/user/Desktop/stage3_sensor_node_enclosure_board.kicad_pcb. Add F.SilkS silkscreen text carrying KICAD_TO_BLENDER, EDGE_FROM_STAGE2_HANDOFF, the stage2 handoff filename, EW4G01, and these board tokens: EW4G01, MCU-U1, USB-C-J1, LED1, LED2, SENSOR-J2. Then use KiCad's plot/export workflow to create the Blender handoff SVG /home/user/Desktop/stage3_sensor_node_enclosure_board_profile.svg from the same Edge.Cuts outline.
4. Blender stage: open Blender. Import /home/user/Desktop/stage2_sensor_node_enclosure.stl with File > Import > STL, then import /home/user/Desktop/stage3_sensor_node_enclosure_board_profile.svg with File > Import > Scalable Vector Graphics (.svg). Keep the imported STL body object and the imported SVG board/profile curves in the scene so the exported GLB carries Blender import evidence such as stage2_sensor_node_enclosure and stage3_sensor_node_enclosure_board_profile.svg. You may leave Blender's default cube/camera/light or remove them; do not manually inject handoff metadata. Export glTF Binary (.glb) as /home/user/Desktop/stage4_sensor_node_enclosure.glb.

Required deliverables on the Desktop: /home/user/Desktop/stage1_sensor_node_enclosure.dxf, /home/user/Desktop/stage2_sensor_node_enclosure.stl, /home/user/Desktop/stage2_sensor_node_enclosure_handoff_outline.dxf, /home/user/Desktop/stage3_sensor_node_enclosure_board.kicad_pcb, /home/user/Desktop/stage3_sensor_node_enclosure_board_profile.svg, /home/user/Desktop/stage4_sensor_node_enclosure.glb.

[Software] Use LibreCAD first, then FreeCAD, then KiCad, then Blender. Do not skip stages, reorder stages, or recreate the final result in only one software package.
